newsitem.title: UK: Thorn 9-month pretax profit rises 8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Thorn 9-month pretax profit rises 8 pct.

text.p: British electric and retail giant Thorn Plc announced an eight percent rise in its pretax profits for the ninght period to December 31, 1996 to 123 million pounds ($199.4 million).
The company, which split last year from music giant EMI said its turnover for the period rose five percent to 1.19 billion stg. The company's return on sales was up to 11.2 percent, the company said.
The company said its third quarter trading performance and the continuing rise in strength of the sterling would reduce the reported value of Thorn's non-UK profits for the current year.
Thorn said it anticipated its current year profits before tax and exceptional items to be broadly unchanged against last year's proforma equivalent of 170.7 million pounds.
Thorn's net borrowings was lower till the end of nine months at 233.7 million stg compared to 260 million stg, proforma, at March 31, 1996.
The company said it was closing down 90 Radio rental stores and opening 60 Crazy George stores, dealing in furniture rentals in the UK.
